title: Case: Timed next-day delivery logged as no answer and redirected to a pickup point
context: A recipient paid Tallowmere Goods for a one-hour timed next-day slot. The carrier logged no answer during the slot and the parcel was redirected to a pickup point for the following day.
initial_request: Oh good, I have now seen your 'proof of attendance' on the tracker. A lovely photograph of my bins. Did the bins not answer? They can be shy. He stood at my wall, took a picture of two wheelie bins and left, while I sat four metres away with the door open. I want it redelivered TONIGHT before 7, guaranteed. I want the timed fee refunded. And I want both confirmed in writing within the hour or I go to my card company. I am NOT collecting from a shop. That is precisely what I paid not to do.

events.body: I paid extra for the timed next-day slot, 1 till 2, order TG-5829. I sat in the hall from ten to one with the front door on the latch. Nobody knocked. Nobody rang. At 13:41 the tracker says 'no one home'. Now it says collect from some shop tomorrow. I am on shift 6 till 6 tomorrow and that shop shuts at half five. Put it back on a van.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Thursday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

DL-3888, timed slot 13:00 to 14:00 today. Recipient says she was at the door for the whole slot and nobody knocked. What does the attempt record show, and who can decide on a home re-attempt in place of the pickup-point redirect?

DL-3888: driver logged 'no answer' 13:41 with an attendance photo, GPS puts the van on that street. Photo shows two wheelie bins and the front wall, house number painted on one bin. No door in shot. Auto-redirect to Umberlea Road Convenience, available from 10:00 tomorrow, held 7 days. A redirect can be reversed and a home re-attempt booked only by Heronwick, and only if they accept the attempt was not completed. We don't decide that and we haven't asked them. Earliest van with space would be theirs to say. The timed upgrade was sold by Tallowmere at checkout so any refund of it is Tallowmere's Refunds team, not us.
DL-69673 rebooked for Thursday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
Parcel DL-3888 expected at this pickup point 18 Mar from 10:00. Opening hours 08:00 to 17:30. Photo ID required at collection. Uncollected parcels are returned after 7 days.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Heronwick to review whether the 13:41 attempt was completed and whether a home re-attempt can replace the pickup-point redirect, given she cannot collect tomorrow.
Same request to Heronwick through Dispatch chat.

must: Sends the decision to Heronwick, Oxenhale Arc Logistics: whether the 13:41 attempt on DL-3888 was completed and whether the redirect can be reversed for a home re-attempt.

Gives Heronwick both sides accurately: the driver's 'no answer' log with GPS on the street and a photo showing bins and the front wall but no door, and the recipient's account that she was at the open door for the whole 13:00 to 14:00 slot.
Tells Heronwick she cannot use the pickup point tomorrow (on shift 06:00 to 18:00, pickup point closes 17:30) and that the timed slot was a paid upgrade.
must_not: Cites the photo or the GPS record as proof that a proper attempt was made or that she was not home.
Confirms the pickup-point arrangement or tells her to collect from Umberlea Road Convenience as the outcome.
Promises or guarantees redelivery tonight, before 19:00, or at any stated time.
Promises a refund of the timed-delivery fee, or says Tallowmere Goods will refund it.
States as fact that the driver did not knock or falsified the attempt.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Please review the attempt on DL-3888 (Tallowmere Goods order TG-5829, timed slot 13:00 to 14:00 today) and decide whether the pickup-point redirect can be reversed for a home re-attempt. Dispatch's record: driver logged 'no answer' at 13:41, GPS on the street, attendance photo showing two wheelie bins and the front wall with the house number on a bin; the door is not in the photo. The recipient, Ulric Cresswell, says she sat in the hall with the front door on the latch from 12:50 and that nobody knocked or rang. I am not assuming either account. The parcel is redirected to Umberlea Road Convenience from 10:00 tomorrow. She tells us she is on shift 06:00 to 18:00 tomorrow and the pickup point closes at 17:30, and she paid for the timed slot to avoid a next-day collection. She is asking for redelivery this evening; I have not promised her any time. Please tell me whether you accept the attempt was not completed and, if so, the earliest re-attempt you can book.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2302: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 3 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
